Subject: Post-call: SLO/Autoscale follow-up (latency targets & burst capacity)

Hi Amit / Jasmine —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap + agreed next steps from our discovery focused on performance SLOs and autoscaling behavior so folks have a single place to reference.

Recap (from the call)
- Target SLOs: 99th percentile generation latency <= 200ms for single-turn prompts (avg prompt length ~60 tokens).
- Concurrency: target peak concurrent requests ~250, sustained baseline 60-80.
- Throughput: spikes up to ~12k requests/min during promos; typical sustained ~2k/min.
- Streaming: partial token streaming required for user experience; must start sending tokens within 50–100ms of generation start.
- Error budget: FastPay wants <0.5% request failure rate and <2% queueing-abort during peaks.

Autoscaling / burst items we discussed
- Warm pool / pre-warmed instances: FastPay asked whether we can keep a small warm pool to reduce cold-starts for bursts.
- Scale-up time: we discussed cold start 30–90s vs warm pool <5–10s.
- Burst capacity: can provision reserved burst GPUs for short windows (5–30m) vs gradual autoscale.
- Queueing: Redwood queues requests when capacity is saturated; policy options: FIFO or priority-based (e.g., premium traffic first) and configurable max queue time before failover.

Action items / owners
- Dev (cc’d): confirm realistic warm-pool sizing and exact warm start latency numbers for our model family, and any tradeoffs for streaming. (Due: 08/06)
- Connor (cc’d): provide recommended batching/throughput config and cost delta for keeping a 10–20% warm pool vs relying on burst GPUs. (Due: 08/07)
- FastPay: share 7-day traffic csv + typical peak windows so we can propose a trial config. Amit/Jasmine to send by EOD 08/05.

Attachments: call recording + SLO proposal template attached.

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick session if you want to review numbers live.

Best,

Hi Amit / Marissa —

Thanks for the call and the clarification. A few technical notes based on the model family you demoed and our runtime behavior:

Warm pool vs cold start
- Cold start (no warm instances): full model load and kernel init can be ~30–90s depending on model size and infra (we saw 45–70s for 13B-class under typical infra).
- Warm pool: keeping pre-initialized model workers (with KV cache primed if desired) yields warm start ~3–8s to accept traffic. Memory footprint is higher (each warm worker uses allocated GPU memory) so there's a cost tradeoff.

Burst / reserved capacity
- Short-lived burst GPUs: we can reserve burst replicas that are already provisioned (reserved for your account during windows). That gives near-instant capacity but increases committed cost for the reserved window.
- Policy: recommend a hybrid: small warm pool sized for 15–20% of expected peak concurrency + burst reserve for the remaining spike headroom. Example: for 250 peak concurrency -> warm pool 40–50 workers, burst reserve to bring total to 300 for 15m windows.

Queueing behavior and SLOs
- Queueing: Redwood uses request queueing at the route-level. Default behavior is FIFO with a configurable max queue time (we propose 10s for UI flows) and a priority override for premium calls. Exceeding queue time will return a 503 unless auto-fallback to a smaller model is enabled.
- Streaming: streaming latency is sensitive to scheduling. We recommend minimum batch size 1 and micro-batching threshold 10ms for UI flows to keep first-token low while still batching when possible.

Next steps proposal
- I'll populate the attached SLO worksheet with warm-pool sizing options and estimated cost delta for a 2-week trial.
- If FastPay is comfortable, we can stand up a 2-week trial with the hybrid config above and monitor: 99p latency, queue time, failure rate, and cost. Need a point of contact to approve short-term burst commit for trial.
